Ghost in the Shell

Mamoru Oshii’s 1995 animated film of Masamune Shirow’s manga, set in a city modelled on Hong Kong, whose opening credits of computer code inspired the digital rain of The Matrix.

Source
Wikipedia: Ghost in the Shell (1995 film)
Creator
Mamoru Oshii (director); Production I.G (animation studio)
Made
1995 (released 18 November 1995 in Japan)
Style
Cyberpunk (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Dystopian, contemplative, nocturnal, high-tech
Evidence
Based on the Wikipedia articles on the film and on cyberpunk, read as wikitext on 2026-10-02. No image of the film was inspected for this record.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: the city of the film was based on Hong Kong. Oshii felt that its streets, where “old and new exist in confusing relationships”, fit the theme of the film. Cyberpunk.

The opening credits were produced by CG director Seichi Tanaka, who converted code in a computer language displayed in romanized Japanese letters. Wikipedia).

The Wachowskis showed the film to producer Joel Silver, saying “We wanna do that for real.” The digital rain of The Matrix was inspired by its opening credits. Wikipedia).

Why it belongs

The film turns code itself into imagery. That is the source of the style’s terminal text used as decoration, which The Matrix website later made a web look.

Its city follows Blade Runner in taking Hong Kong as the model, which makes Hong Kong streets the most common real reference for the style.

Borrow

Use real-looking code or data as a texture behind a title, in one color, and keep it legible.

Show the cyborg theme through interface overlays on a body or face, not through ornament.
